subject: general
question: According to a March 2025 PIB report, India's defence production reached ₹1.27 trillion in FY 2023-24, showing an increase of what percentage from FY 2014-15?
solution:
The correct answer is **174%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's defence production in the financial year 2023-24 reached ₹1.27 trillion, showcasing a significant rise in the sector.
 
• According to reports, this marks a **1.74 times increase in defence production** compared to the financial year 2014-15.
 
• The growth is attributed to the government's initiatives such as the 'Make in India' campaign, aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing in the defence sector.
 
• The Ministry of Defence has consistently pushed for indigenization of defence equipment, reducing dependence on imports, and boosting domestic production.
 
• Between FY 2014-15 and FY 2023-24, the Indian government has introduced several reforms, including providing incentives to private players, increasing defence budgets, and establishing defence corridors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defence Production in India**

 
 
• India has been focusing on becoming a global defence manufacturing hub, with an emphasis on indigenization and self-reliance.
 
• Key policies such as the Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020 and the establishment of Defence Industrial Corridors (DICs) have been instrumental in achieving this growth.
 
• The government has also increased Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) limits in the defence sector to 74% through the automatic route and 100% via government approval.
 
• Major defence PSUs such as Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) have significantly contributed to this growth.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative**
 
 
• Launched in September 2014, this initiative aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub.
 
• Under this initiative, the defence sector has been identified as a priority sector for boosting domestic manufacturing.
 
• It has encouraged private sector participation and partnerships with global Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) for technology transfer and co-production.
